comments.text: I just donated my kidney 3 months ago, since I wasn’t a direct match with my partner, we participated in the paired kidney exchange program.  So I did donate to a stranger and it also benefited someone close to me, I guess you could call it the best of both worlds.  I went in Thursday morning and was discharged Saturday afternoon, everything was paid by the recipient insurance, and my work graciously offered 6 weeks of organ donation leave for recovery.  It took a while for my body to feel close to 100% (my abdomen still feels tender and healing), but like Jesse stated I’ve not experienced any negative impact to my quality of life as someone with one kidney.  Seeing firsthand how debilitating it can be to be on dialysis, it is truly a gift of life to donate your second kidney that the majority of us can live (and thrive) without.

comments.text:
Thank you so much for doing these interviews. My dad recieved a liver from a deceased donor in January 2014 after spending most of December in the hospital with liver failure due to Autoimmune Hepatitis. He was then a kidney recipient in October 2019 due to kidney failure from Diabetes caused by decades of medication to manage the liver issues. My dad has been sick for nearly 40 years and organ transplantation saved his life TWICE! I was a freshman in college when he got the liver which allowed him to see me graduate, get a job, and start adulthood. He got to witness my sister find her now husband. He got his kidney transplant barely a month before her wedding. He got to walk her down the aisle. He got to see her become a mother twice over. He was around to help save my life when I went through a crisis in 2024 and had to be hospitalized for my own safety. Organ transplantation doesn't just save the lives of the recipient but also their families. 

We don't know the donor in either case but the kidney was able to happen because my aunt (my dad's sister) was willing to donate. She wasn't a direct match but she was willing to be a part of a donation chain! She went in for sugery in the morning when the other donors from across the country went in. Her kidney was then transported to the recipient (unknown to our family). Later that afternoon my dad went in for surgery after his kidney arrived (unknown origin point but donated by a living donor as a part of a train of non-direct donors).
My family was changed for the better because of organ donation and transplantation. It was HARD and honestly, a bit traumatic to go through! But I will always be grateful for both of the donors for giving me extra time with my dad.
